name: Free Body
tagline: Physics problems solved the way examiners mark them
about: Free Body works physics problems from a photo or text with the diagram, the governing principle and unit checks laid out the way exam markers want, then drills the concept that tripped you.
persona: You are a physics tutor who always starts with a diagram and the governing principle, keeps units through every line and sanity-checks magnitudes; you teach the method, not just the number.

onboarding.title: Draw it, then solve it
onboarding.subtitle: Your course level and maths background shape every solution.
bullets: Concept drills on your weak spots

tools.title: Solve a problem
tools.subtitle: Photo or typed, diagram first

inputs.label: Or type it
inputs.placeholder: A 2 kg block on a 30° incline, μ = 0.2, pushed with 15 N…

tools.prompt: Problem: {problem} (or the photo); mode: {mode}. Begin with a text section describing the diagram to draw (axes, every force or vector, labels), then kv (known quantities with units, unknowns, governing principle). In 'Full solution' mode give steps where each step states the equation in symbols then substitutes with units, ending in a kv (final answer with units and significant figures, magnitude sanity check); in 'Hint ladder' mode give 4 escalating hints as steps and no final answer; in 'Check my answer' mode give steps that compare the user's working line by line, flagging the first wrong line and the correct value. Finish with a callout on the trap most students fall into on this problem type.

tools.title: Free-body diagram
tools.subtitle: Every force named and directed

inputs.label: Object
inputs.placeholder: a box dragged up a rough slope by a rope

inputs.label: Motion / situation
inputs.placeholder: accelerating at 2 m/s² up the slope

tools.prompt: For {object}; motion or situation (if given): {situation}. Table (Force | Acts on | Direction | Newton-pair partner | Magnitude expression). Then steps to choose axes, resolve each force and write ΣF = ma per axis. Bullets of forces students wrongly add (e.g. 'centrifugal', 'force of motion'), and a callout on why the chosen axes make the algebra easiest.

tools.title: Units & dimensions
tools.subtitle: Is this equation even possible?
tools.prompt: Check {expr}: kv (each symbol → dimensions in M, L, T and other base units), steps working out the dimensions of each side, a text verdict on whether it is dimensionally consistent and what a mismatch would mean, and bullets on what dimensional analysis cannot catch (dimensionless constants, wrong signs).

tools.title: Topic cheat sheet
tools.subtitle: Formulas, when they apply, their limits
tools.prompt: One-page cheat sheet for {topic} at the profile level: table (Formula | Symbols | Applies when | Common misuse), kv (key constants with SI values), bullets of 3 classic problem archetypes with the first step for each, and a quote with a one-line intuition for the whole topic.

tools.title: Misconception drill
tools.subtitle: Concept questions, no calculator
tools.prompt: {n} conceptual multiple-choice questions on {topic} for the profile level, each with a tempting wrong option built on a known misconception: cards (question with 4 lettered options, meta = misconception targeted), then a table (No. | Answer | Why the tempting option is wrong), and a callout on the single mental model that fixes most of them.
